heroHeadline: Lebanon-Israel Round 4 (June 2–3): Rubio Calls Aoun & Netanyahu June 1, Tables Phased Plan; US-Iran Deal Day 4 Unsigned as Trump Returns Amended Drafts; Hormuz Still Closed
heroSubtitle: June 1, 2026 — Secretary of State Rubio held separate calls with Lebanese President Aoun and Israeli PM Netanyahu on June 1 to prepare Round 4 political-track talks in Washington (June 2–3), tabling a phased de-escalation proposal: Hezbollah halts all attacks; Israel refrains from Beirut escalation. The talks aim to bridge the core impasse — IDF withdrawal from southern Lebanon vs. Hezbollah disarmament south of the Litani — before the 45-day ceasefire extension expires around June 29. On the US-Iran front, President Trump returned amended MOU drafts to Tehran on June 1 seeking stricter nuclear commitments and expanded Strait of Hormuz reopening guarantees, pushing any formal signing back by at least another week. The IAEA reported on May 31 that Iran has amassed a record amount of military-grade enriched uranium — adding pressure on both sides to close the deal. The Strait of Hormuz remains physically closed: ~750 vessels trapped, ~$6B/month in Iranian oil exports blocked, US gas prices at ~$4.48/gallon. Colombia's ELN 4-day election ceasefire holds into Day 2 with no violations; Cepeda and De la Espriella open their June 21 runoff campaigns with peace architecture as the defining axis — Cepeda pledges to restart ELN talks and continue JEP; De la Espriella pledges to terminate all negotiations immediately.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
